Tropical Cyclone Bulletin #4
  • Super Typhoon "Rosal"

Super Typhoon "Rosal"

Issued at 05:00 am, 21 October 2026
(Valid for broadcast until the next advisory to be issued at 11:00 AM today)

SUPER TYPHOON ROSAL ACCELERATES WHILE OVER THE SEA EAST OF NORTHERN LUZON.
  • HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND AREAS
  • Heavy Rainfall Outlook
  •  
  • Refer to Weather Advisory No. 3 issued at 5:00 AM today for the heavy rainfall outlook due to the TC ROSAL.
  • Severe Winds
  •  
  • The wind signals warn the public of the general wind threat over an area due to the tropical cyclone. Local winds may be slightly stronger/enhanced in coastal and upland/mountainous areas exposed to winds. Winds are less strong in areas sheltered from the prevailing wind direction.
  •  
  • Minimal to minor impacts from strong winds are possible within any of the areas under Wind Signal No. 1.
  • The highest Wind Signal that may be raised during the passage of ROSAL is Wind Signal No. 2 or 3.
  •  
  • The Northeasterly Windflow and the periphery of ROSAL will bring strong to gale-force gusts over the following areas (especially in coastal and upland areas exposed to winds):
  • Today (21 October): Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, Cagayan Valley, Bicol Region, Romblon, Eastern Visayas, Siquijor, Bohol, Northern Mindanao, Caraga, Davao Region, and Sarangani.
  • Tomorrow (22 October): Most of Luzon and Visayas, Zamboanga del Norte, Northern Mindanao, Agusan del Norte, Surigao del Norte, Dinagat Islands, Sarangani, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental.
  • Friday (23 October): Most of Luzon and Visayas, Camiguin, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental.
  • HAZARDS AFFECTING COASTAL WATERS
  • A Gale Warning is in effect over the northern and eastern seaboards of Luzon and the eastern seaboard of Visayas. For more details, refer to Gale Warning No. 2 issued at 5:00 AM today
  • 24-Hour Sea Condition Outlook
  • Up to very rough seas over the following coastal waters:
  • Up to 8.0 m: The seaboards of Batanes; the northern and eastern seaboards of Cagayan including Babuyan Islands.
  • Up to 6.0 m: The remaining seaboards of Cagayan; the seaboard of Isabela.
  • Up to 5.0 m: The eastern seaboard of northern Aurora; the northern and eastern seaboards of Catanduanes
  • Up to 4.5 m: The remaining seaboards of Aurora; the northern and eastern seaboards of Polillo Islands; the northern seaboards of Camarines Norte, Camarines Sur, and Northern Samar; the eastern seaboards of Albay and Sorsogon;
  • Sea travel is risky for all types or tonnage of vessels. All mariners must remain in port or, if underway, seek shelter or safe harbor as soon as possible until winds and waves subside.
  • Up to rough seas over the following coastal waters:
  • Up to 4.0 m: The eastern seaboards of northern Quezon and Eastern Samar; the remaining seaboard of Northern Samar; the northern seaboard of Ilocos Norte.
  • Up to 3.0 m: The eastern seaboards of Dinagat Islands, Siargao-Bucas Grande Island Group, and Davao Oriental; the remaining seaboards of Catanduanes and Ilocos Norte.
  • Mariners of small seacrafts, including all types of motorbancas, are advised not to venture out to sea under these conditions, especially if inexperienced of operating ill-equipped vessels.
  • Up to moderate to rough seas over the following coastal waters:
  • Up to 2.5 m: The seaboards of Ilocos Sur, La Union, Surigao del Sur, and Surigao del Norte; the southern seaboard of Davao Oriental; the remaining eastern seaboards of Quezon; the northwestern seaboard of Pangasinan.
  • Up to 2.0 m: The eastern seaboard of Davao Occidental.
  • Mariners of motorbancas and similarly sized vessels are advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.
  • Other coastal waters have forecast wave heights of less than 2.0 m.
  • TRACK AND INTENSITY OUTLOOK
  • It must be emphasized that heavy rainfall and severe winds may still be experienced in localities outside the landfall point and the forecast confidence cone. Refer to “Other Hazards affecting Land Areas” for more details. Furthermore, the track may still shift within the limit of the forecast confidence cone.
  • ROSAL will continue moving west northwestward today, then northwestward until Friday (23 October) morning, before recurving northeastward by Sunday (25 October). On the forecast track, the tropical cyclone will be closest to Extreme Northern Luzon between tomorrow and Friday afternoon. It will exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) by Friday evening or Saturday (24 October) early morning.
  • Further intensification remains possible within the next 6 hours as ROSAL moves over the Philippine Sea before a weakening trend begins. It is forecast to weaken into a typhoon tomorrow and into a severe tropical storm by Sunday.
Location of Eye/center

The center of the eye of Super Typhoon ROSAL was estimated based on all available data at 990 km East of Northern Luzon (17.6 °N, 131.1 °E )

Movement

Moving West Northwestward at 30 km/h

Strength

Maximum sustained winds of 215 km/h near the center and gustiness of up to 265 km/h

  • Oct 21, 2026 02:00 PM - 790 km East of Aparri, Cagayan
  • Oct 22, 2026 02:00 AM - 550 km East of Basco, Batanes
  • Oct 22, 2026 02:00 PM - 405 km East of Itbayat, Batanes
  • Oct 23, 2026 02:00 AM - 340 km East Northeast of Itbayat, Batanes
  • Oct 23, 2026 02:00 PM - 420 km North Northeast of Itbayat, Batanes
  • Oct 24, 2026 02:00 AM - 565 km North Northeast of Itbayat, Batanes (OUTSIDE PAR)
  • Oct 25, 2026 02:00 AM - 970 km North Northeast of Extreme Northern Luzon (OUTSIDE PAR)
Wind Signal (Areas with TCWS)
Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal no.
Affected Areas
  • Luzon
    • Batanes, Babuyan Islands, mainland Cagayan, the eastern portion of Isabela (Maconacon, Divilacan, Palanan, Santa Maria, Cabagan, Delfin Albano, Santo Tomas, Tumauini, San Pablo, Ilagan City, San Mariano, Dinapigue), the northern and central portions of Apayao (Calanasan, Luna, Santa Marcela, Flora, Pudtol, Kabugao), the northeastern portion of Ilocos Norte (Pagudpud, Adams), and the northeastern portion of Catanduanes (Pandan, Bagamanoc, Panganiban, Viga, Gigmoto)
  • Visayas
    • -
  • Mindanao
    • -
Meteorological Condition
  • A tropical cyclone will affect the locality.
  • Winds of 39-61 km/h may be expected in at least 36 hours or intermittent rains may be expected within 36 hours. (When the tropical cyclone develops very close to the locality a shorter lead time of the occurrence of the winds will be specified in the warning bulletin.)
Impact of the Wind
  • Very light or no damage to low risk structures.
  • Light damage to medium to high risk structures.
  • Slight damage to some houses of very light materials or makeshift structures in exposed communities. Some banana plants are tilted, a few downed and leaves are generally damaged.
  • Twigs of small trees may be broken.
  • Rice crops, however, may suffer significant damage when it is in its flowering stage.
Precautionary Measures
  • When the tropical cyclone is strong or is intensifying and is moving closer, this signal may be upgraded to the next higher level.
  • The waves on coastal waters may gradually develop and become bigger and higher.
  • The people are advised to listen to the latest severe weather bulletin issued by PAGASA every six hours. In the meantime, business may be carried out as usual except when flood occur.
  • Disaster preparedness is activated to alert status.
What To Do
  • Inspect your house if necessary repair/fixing is needed.
  • Clean up drainage system.
  • Harvest crops tha can be yielded.
  • Monitor the latest Severe Weather Bulletin issued By PAGASA every six hours and hourly updates.
    Considering these developments, the public and disaster risk reduction and management offices concerned are advised to take all necessary measures to protect life and property. Persons living in areas identified to be highly or very highly susceptible to these hazards are advised to follow evacuation and other instructions from local officials. For heavy rainfall warnings, thunderstorm/rainfall advisories, and other severe weather information specific to your area, please monitor products issued by your local PAGASA Regional Services Division.
